overtraining.name: Overtraining
overtraining.description: Excessive physical activity without adequate rest leads to both physical and mental fatigue.

lackOfRecovery.name: Lack of Recovery
lackOfRecovery.description: Insufficient recovery times increase the risk of both physical injury and mental exhaustion.

poorNutrition.name: Poor Nutrition
poorNutrition.description: Inadequate nutrition can result in fatigue, poor performance, and greater susceptibility to injury.

improperTechnique.name: Improper Technique
improperTechnique.description: Incorrect form during training or competition can lead to injury and exhaustion.
causes: X factors (improper landing, movement not aligned with rhythm)
Training method by uncertified or non-professionals

externalPressures.name: External Pressures
externalPressures.description: Expectations from coaches, family, stakeholders, and fans can create mental stress.

environmentalConditions.name: Environmental Conditions
environmentalConditions.description: Exercising in extreme temperatures can accelerate physical fatigue, with potential heat exhaustion or heat stroke.
causes: Humidity, heavy rain, extreme heat, winter

monotonyInTraining.name: Monotony in Training
monotonyInTraining.description: Repetitive drills or the same training routine can lead to both physical and mental fatigue due to lack of variety and motivation.
causes: More training, lesser recovery and athlete treatment

activeRecovery.name: Active Recovery
activeRecovery.description: Engaging in low-intensity exercise post-training (like stretching or swimming) can help muscles recover faster.
recommendations: Light cardio activities like swimming or cycling
Stretching routines focusing on worked muscles

adequateSleep.name: Adequate Sleep
adequateSleep.description: Ensuring 7-9 hours of restful sleep is crucial for muscle repair, mental recovery, and overall performance.
recommendations: Create optimal sleep environment (dark, cool, quiet)
Avoid caffeine and heavy meals before sleep

nutritionAndHydration.name: Nutrition and Hydration
nutritionAndHydration.description: A balanced diet rich in proteins, carbs, fats, vitamins, and minerals, along with proper hydration, is essential for energy replenishment.
recommendations: Proper timing of pre and post-workout nutrition
Individualized nutrition plans based on training load

mentalTraining.name: Mental Training
mentalTraining.description: Incorporating mindfulness, meditation, and mental relaxation techniques can help athletes manage stress and prevent burnout.

periodization.name: Periodization
periodization.description: Structuring training to include rest periods and lower-intensity phases to avoid overtraining and allow for physical and mental recovery.
recommendations: Structured training cycles with built-in recovery periods
Varied intensity levels throughout training phases
Alternating focus between different fitness components
Individual periodization plans based on response to training

psychologicalSupport.name: Psychological Support
psychologicalSupport.description: Working with sports psychologists can help athletes manage anxiety, stress, and emotional fatigue, while improving mental resilience.
recommendations: Team-building activities to improve support network

achillesTendon.name: Achilles Tendon
achillesTendon.description: Your Achilles tendon is the thick cord that connects your calf muscles to your heel bone.

commonInjuries.name: Achilles Tendinitis
symptoms: Pain and stiffness along the tendon

commonInjuries.name: Achilles Tendon Rupture
symptoms: Sudden, sharp pain in the back of the ankle

ankleJoint.name: Ankle Joint
ankleJoint.description: Your ankle contains three joints, as well as other bones, cartilage, ligaments, muscles and tendons.

elbowJoint.name: Elbow Joint
elbowJoint.description: Your elbow joint is prone to overuse injuries from repetitive movements during sports.

commonInjuries.name: Tennis Elbow
symptoms: Pain on the outer side of the elbow
Pain when lifting or bending arm

commonInjuries.name: Golfer's Elbow
symptoms: Pain and tenderness on the inner side of elbow

commonInjuries.name: Elbow Bursitis
symptoms: Swelling at the tip of the elbow

head.name: Head
head.description: Less than 2 in 10 sports injuries are head injuries, but they can include nosebleeds, tooth loss, and concussions.

kneeJoint.name: Knee Joint
kneeJoint.description: Your knee joint includes several ligaments that you can sprain.

commonInjuries.name: PCL Tear
symptoms: Pain in the back of the knee

commonInjuries.name: Meniscal Tear
symptoms: Pain when twisting or rotating knee

legMuscles.name: Leg Muscles
legMuscles.description: Leg muscle strains are common in various sports activities.

commonInjuries.name: Groin Pull
symptoms: Pain and tenderness in the groin and thigh area

commonInjuries.name: Hamstring Strain
symptoms: Sudden sharp pain in the back of the thigh
Inability to put weight on leg

commonInjuries.name: Shin Splint
symptoms: Pain along the inner edge of the shinbone

shoulderJoint.name: Shoulder Joint
shoulderJoint.description: Injuries to your shoulder's rotator cuff and other structures.

commonInjuries.name: Rotator Cuff Tear
symptoms: Dull ache deep in the shoulder

commonInjuries.name: Shoulder Tendinitis
symptoms: Pain that increases with overhead activities

commonInjuries.name: Swimmer's Shoulder
symptoms: Pain when arm is raised overhead

otherInjuries.name: Other Common Injuries
otherInjuries.description: Other common sports injuries that may occur in various body regions.

commonInjuries.name: Bone Fracture
symptoms: Inability to bear weight or use the limb
